title: Feasibility of a participatively developed physiotherapeutic training program to improve activity and training-related control competence of people with Low Back Pain (LBP)
summary:
Exercise and its dosage play an important role in the management of patients with LBP. Exercise control (including volume, intensity, rest periods) and the management of physical resources, known as pacing, play an important role in both structured training (such as strength training) and everyday aerobic activities (such as walking). 
The authors' previous research results illustrate the complexity of the topic and suggest that decisions on load management and pacing descisions are made on the basis of a variety of factors, but may not be sufficiently individualized.  
The aim of this feasibility study is to develop a specific training concept for physiotherapists to optimize pacing and load control of strength training and aerobic activities, to pilot the training program and evaluate its feasibility in the practice setting. It also aims to determine whether targeted training of the physiotherapists has an impact on patient-relevant outcomes.

interventions.name: Physiotherapists in the intervention group will receive approximately 3 hours of online training and additional materials to provide to their patients. They will be encouraged to incorporate the training contents into the management of their patients with LBP and will receive support from the resear

Physiotherapists in the control group do not receive any training initially. At the end of the trial, they will be given access to all the materials and the Powerpoint presentation of the training program. During the study, they treat their patients with LBP as usual.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Practices and facilities whose physiotherapists regularly treat or have treated patients with low back pain (on average at least once a week for six months or 20 times in their working life) are included. Participating physiotherapists may be employed full-time or part-time but should work as a physiotherapist for at least 15 hours per week.
Patients must be between the ages of 18 and 65. They must have episodic or chronic low back pain.
Exclusion criteria:
Failure to fulfil the inclusion criteria leads to exclusion. 
Patients whose complaints result from structural pathologies (e.g. infections, tumors, osteoporosis, fractures or deformities of the lumbar spine, inflammatory diseases, radiculopathies, or cauda equina syndrome) are excluded.
Patients who can only lift or carry very light weights or nothing at all or who need to use a cane or forearm crutches because of pain (items from the Oswestry Disability Index) are excluded.
Patients with an average pain intensity of 8 out of 10 or more on the NRS are also excluded.
